# exploreDE

[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/fgcz/exploreDE/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/fgcz/exploreDE/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)

exploreDE is a Shiny app for exploring differential expression results
from RNA-seq, proteomics and CRISPR screens, and for making
publication-quality figures from them: ordination plots, heatmaps,
volcano plots, box plots, GO and KEGG pathway views, ORA and GSEA
results, and comparisons across contrasts.

It opens an AnnData `.h5ad` file in the exploreDE/1.0 layout, which
[`build_explore_h5ad()`](https://fgcz.github.io/exploreDE/reference/build_explore_h5ad.md)
writes from the results of any pipeline (DESeq2, edgeR, limma, prolfqua,
SAINTexpress), and the results of the FGCZ SUSHI and prolfqua pipelines.

Documentation: <https://fgcz.github.io/exploreDE/>

## Installation

exploreDE is submitted to Bioconductor. Until it is released there,
install it from GitHub:

``` r
install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("fgcz/exploreDE") # needs Bioconductor >= 3.23 (anndataR >= 1.2.3)
```

Once it is on Bioconductor:

``` r
BiocManager::install("exploreDE")
```

Optional: KEGG pathway views, GLM-PCA, and formatted group labels.
Without these packages the app hides the feature or shows plain text.

``` r
BiocManager::install(c("pathview", "glmpca", "ggtext", "gridtext"))
```

## Quick start

``` r
library(exploreDE)
exploreDE()                            # landing page: upload a file or load the demo dataset
exploreDE("my_data.h5ad")              # open a file directly
exploreDE(c("a.h5ad", "b.h5ad"))       # compare the contrasts of several files
exploreDE(se)                          # open a SummarizedExperiment or AnnData object
```

The menu shows only the tabs your data supports: DE tabs need a DE
table, pathway tabs need enrichment results.

## Documentation

- [`vignette("exploreDE")`](https://fgcz.github.io/exploreDE/articles/exploreDE.md):
  the app’s tabs, and opening a dataset in R
- [`vignette("bring-your-own-data", package = "exploreDE")`](https://fgcz.github.io/exploreDE/articles/bring-your-own-data.md):
  building a file from your own results: counts only, proteomics,
  RNA-seq with pathways, organisms without an annotation package, and
  unrecognised column names
- [`?build_explore_h5ad`](https://fgcz.github.io/exploreDE/reference/build_explore_h5ad.md):
  the argument reference
- `system.file("spec/exploreDE-h5ad-1.0.md", package = "exploreDE")`:
  the `.h5ad` format, for writing files from Python or another tool
- `system.file("skills/exploreDE-byod/SKILL.md", package = "exploreDE")`:
  give this to an AI assistant to have it write the import script for
  your data

## Bring your own data

Only counts, a sample table and the omics type are required; DE tables
and pathway results are optional.

``` r
build_explore_h5ad(
  counts,                                   # features x samples matrix
  out     = "my_data.h5ad",
  omics   = "rnaseq",                       # or "proteomics", "crispr"
  coldata = coldata,                        # one row per sample, rownames = colnames(counts)
  rowdata = annotation,                     # optional: gene ids, symbols, GO terms, ...
  de      = list(Treat_vs_Ctrl = de_table)  # optional: one table per contrast
)
```

You don’t need to rename columns: a dictionary recognises the usual
DESeq2, edgeR, limma, prolfqua and SAINTexpress names, and warns when it
can’t place one. The prolfquapp DEA’s `AnnData.h5ad` (prolfquapp 2.10.x)
opens as it is.

## Saving your settings

The **Save / Load Session** tab downloads your settings across every tab
(widgets, the feature bucket, pathway selections and Multi DE datasets)
as one `.json` file, and restores them on the same dataset later. It
holds no data. Format:
`system.file("spec/exploreDE-session-2.md", package = "exploreDE")`.

## Running on a server

On a server, `?data=` opens a dataset from the link:

- `?data=<result directory>`: a SUSHI result on FGCZ’s gStore
  (LDAP-checked)
- `?data=<percent-encoded https link to an .h5ad>`: a file from an
  allowed source (by default APB Export jobs and public pStore; set
  `EXPLOREDE_URL_SOURCES` to change the list). Plain `https://` only, no
  redirects, up to 1 GB.

The LDAP check takes the user from the `SHINYPROXY_USERNAME` environment
variable, read once per R process, so run the app behind ShinyProxy with
one container per user. Without that variable (plain Shiny Server, for
example) every gStore link is refused; the demo, uploads and `https://`
links still work.

## Getting help

- Questions: <https://support.bioconductor.org>, tag `exploreDE`
- Bugs and feature requests: <https://github.com/fgcz/exploreDE/issues>

## AI use and provenance

AI coding agents helped write this package:

- Tools: Claude Code (Anthropic), and in-house open-weight models such
  as Qwen
- Extent: the review fixes, refactoring, tests and documentation of the
  Bioconductor submission in late 2026; the app itself was written from
  2025 on by Peter Leary and contributors
- Marking: commits written with AI help carry an
  `Assisted-by: AI coding agent` trailer since 2 November 2026; earlier
  commits are not marked, so treat the whole code base as AI-assisted
- Review: the maintainer reviewed every change before committing it
- Testing: the testthat suite covers the dataset classes, the `.h5ad`
  builder and reader, and the session format; shinytest2 tests drive the
  app in a browser; R CMD check, BiocCheck, lintr and the browser tests
  run in CI on every push

Provenance and licence:

- No code is copied from other software projects
- The example datasets and their sources are listed in
  [`inst/examples/README.md`](https://fgcz.github.io/exploreDE/inst/examples/README.md)
- Anthropic’s terms assign the rights in generated output to the user,
  and the open-weight models’ licences claim no rights in it, so all
  code can be redistributed under this package’s MIT licence

The maintainer is responsible for all code in this package, whatever
helped write it, and for its reliability and maintenance.

# Package index

## Run the app

- [`exploreDE()`](https://fgcz.github.io/exploreDE/reference/exploreDE.md)
  : Start the exploreDE app

## Build and check exploreDE files

Write an `.h5ad` in the exploreDE/1.0 layout, open it as a dataset, and
check it.

- [`build_explore_h5ad()`](https://fgcz.github.io/exploreDE/reference/build_explore_h5ad.md)
  :

  Build a canonical exploreDE `.h5ad` from user-supplied data

- [`new_explore_dataset()`](https://fgcz.github.io/exploreDE/reference/new_explore_dataset.md)
  :

  Construct an `ExploreDataset` instance from a path, URL, or SE

- [`validate_explore_dataset()`](https://fgcz.github.io/exploreDE/reference/validate_explore_dataset.md)
  :

  Runtime validator for a live `ExploreDataset` instance

## Dataset classes

The accessor API the app reads every dataset through, one class per
storage backend.

- [`ExploreDataset`](https://fgcz.github.io/exploreDE/reference/ExploreDataset.md)
  : Abstract base class for exploreDE's storage-agnostic dataset wrapper

- [`ExploreDatasetH5AD`](https://fgcz.github.io/exploreDE/reference/ExploreDatasetH5AD.md)
  :

  Concrete `ExploreDataset` backend over a canonical AnnData (`.h5ad`)

- [`ExploreDatasetSE`](https://fgcz.github.io/exploreDE/reference/ExploreDatasetSE.md)
  : Abstract intermediate class for SE-backed datasets

- [`ExploreDatasetSE_CountQC`](https://fgcz.github.io/exploreDE/reference/ExploreDatasetSE_CountQC.md)
  :

  Concrete subclass for SUSHI CountQC `SummarizedExperiment` outputs

- [`ExploreDatasetSE_CrisprCountQC`](https://fgcz.github.io/exploreDE/reference/ExploreDatasetSE_CrisprCountQC.md)
  : Concrete subclass for CRISPR Mageck CountQC outputs

- [`ExploreDatasetSE_Proteomics`](https://fgcz.github.io/exploreDE/reference/ExploreDatasetSE_Proteomics.md)
  :

  Concrete subclass for FGCZ proteomics `SummarizedExperiment` outputs

- [`ExploreDatasetSE_RNASeq`](https://fgcz.github.io/exploreDE/reference/ExploreDatasetSE_RNASeq.md)
  :

  Concrete subclass for SUSHI RNA-seq `SummarizedExperiment` outputs
